title: Dittany: Contribution-Guided Repair Framework for MAS Applications
abstract: arXiv:2610.42144v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: LLM-based multi-agent system (MAS) applications can produce useful intermediate results while leaving task requirements unsatisfied. Repairing such executions requires identifying the work still needed and the completed results that can support it. We present \tool, a contribution-guided runtime repair framework for MAS applications. \tool derives expected contributions and acceptance conditions from task requirements and method specifications, and connects their dependencies in a contribution graph. Runtime checks locate unmet conditions and establish which results remain usable. These results guide action-level correction when available inputs suffice, or graph-level recovery when prerequisites or unfinished work need revision. Both repair scopes retain validated contributions and check repaired outputs before subsequent work uses them. We evaluate \tool on 30 applications across six MAS frameworks and 9,000 tasks. translated_title: Dittany：面向多智能体系统（MAS）应用的贡献引导式修复框架
translated_abstract: 基于大语言模型（LLM）的多智能体系统（MAS）应用在产生有用中间结果的同时，可能仍未能满足任务需求。修复此类执行过程需要识别出尚待完成的工作，以及能够支持这些工作的已完成结果。我们提出了 Dittany，一个面向 MAS 应用的贡献引导式运行时修复框架。Dittany 从任务需求和方法规范中推导出预期贡献与接受条件，并将它们的依赖关系连接成一张贡献图。运行时检查用于定位未满足的条件，并确定哪些结果仍然可用。当可用输入足够时，这些结果可引导动作级修正；当前置条件或未完成的工作需要修订时，则引导图级恢复。两种修复范围都会保留已验证的贡献，并在后续工作使用修复后的输出之前对其进行检查。我们在六个 MAS 框架上的 30 个应用和 9,000 个任务上对 Dittany 进行了评估，它能够检测运行时故障……
tldr: Dittany 通过从任务需求中构建贡献图来追踪多智能体系统中已完成的有效结果与未满足的接受条件，从而在运行时实现动作级修正和图级恢复，在保留有效贡献的同时修复未满足任务需求的执行过程。
